A1.justification: Both complete 36-page PDFs describe the same research. Their text, equations, four figures, six tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching proofs relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical approximation guarantees and proofs. Its plots and numerical case-analysis tables support mathematical arguments, not original experiments, simulations, or empirical data analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the theoretical algorithms, bounds, and mathematical case analyses. Neither the main text nor the appendix reports original empirical results.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2, the LP formulations, and rounding functions (11)–(13) are unchanged. Pivot selection, majority-color assignment, and rounding parameters remain identical.

E1.justification: Both versions address the same pseudometric-weighted and chromatic correlation-clustering problems. Neither uses datasets or empirical training and evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Section 4.3 retains the same theoretical comparisons with Charikar and Gao's LP-UMVD-Pivot and Xiu et al.'s CCC method. No empirical comparator evaluations are added or removed.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an empirical evaluation protocol. Parameters and configurations used in the mathematical comparisons and case analyses are unchanged.

E4.justification: No ablation, robustness, sensitivity, or empirical case-study experiments are added or removed. The apparent additional analysis in v2 Section 4.4 is the proof already present in v1 Appendix A.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Expected-cost guarantees concern theoretical randomized algorithms and remain unchanged.

E6.justification: The reported approximation bounds, numerical proof evaluations, and entries in Tables 1–6 match. Relocation and renumbering introduce no new results or changed numerical findings.

T1.justification: The four theorems, six lemmas, assumptions, and derivations are retained. v1 Appendix A becomes v2 Section 4.4, while v1 Appendix B becomes v2 Appendix A; these moves do not change the proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a tight 10/3 approximation within the stated pseudometric-weighted framework and a 2.15 approximation for CCC with a 2.11 lower bound in the same analytical framework.

C2.justification: The framework-specific optimality and near-optimality interpretations, explanations of tailored rounding, and treatment of neutral edges remain unchanged. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added.

D1.justification: Both provide the same pseudocode, LP constraints, and explicit rounding parameters. No implementation instructions, hardware information, runtime measurements, or code/data access information are added or removed.

R1.justification: The same 32 works and research positioning are retained. The formerly authorless 'Clustering with qualitative information' entry, v1 reference 1, gains its authors as v2 reference 15; this is a bibliographic repair, not a new citation.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the CCC related-work paragraph, removes repeated acronym expansions, alphabetizes the authors with an explanatory footnote, and repairs a reference entry. It also moves Appendix A into Section 4.4 and relabels the remaining appendix.

P2.justification: All four figures and six tables are retained. Figure 4 is enlarged and separated from Table 4; the former Appendix A diagram and Tables 1–3 move into Section 4.4, with associated renumbering and page reflow.

improvement.justification: The larger Figure 4 makes its region labels easier to read, and the repaired reference restores missing author attribution. These modest presentation gains outweigh the small new 'Appendix 4.4' reference-label error. The algorithms, guarantees, and proofs remain unchanged.
